paper.title: Beyond Reward Suppression: Near-Optimal Offline Attacks on Warm-Start Bandits with Bounded Rewards

settings.name_in_paper: Bounded offline attacks on warm-start stochastic bandits
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Guarantees are for an attacker (data-poisoning attack cost on a bandit learner), not for the learner.
unmapped: Objective is the attacker's cost (number of injected fake action-reward samples) needed to make the learner pull a target arm in (nearly) all online rounds; not regret
Warm-start: learner initialised with an offline log; attacker injects valid bounded-reward samples only before deployment
Attacker observes clean offline log and knows learner's policy, T and reward range [r_min, r_max]
Rewards supported on [r_min, r_max] and sigma^2-sub-Gaussian with known sigma
settings.definition_quote: We consider a stochastic multi-armed bandit with arm set $\mathcal K$ ... Rewards are supported on $[\rl,\ru]$ and are $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian, where $\sigma^2$ is known to the learner. The learner is initialized with an offline log ... The attack cost is the number of injected samples.

algorithms.name: Bounded offline injection attack on warm-start UCB
Bounded offline injection attack on Thompson Sampling
Bounded offline injection attack on epsilon-greedy

symbols.eps_lcb: varepsilon = (lower confidence bound on target mean from clean log) - r_min

conditions: R = Theta(1), sigma = Theta(1), N_i^cl = Theta(1) (Assumption 4.1)
learner is UCB with bonus 3 sigma sqrt(log t / N_i(t))

source.label: thm:attack-cost-ucb
source.quote: Fix $\delta\in(0,1/2)$. Under~\Cref{asp:scaling-assumptions}, for all sufficiently large $T$, the above attack satisfies $\Pr(\sum_{i=1}^{K-1} N_i^\on (T+1) = 0) \ge 1 - \delta$ and $\mathcal C(\mathbf n) = \mathcal O(\frac{K \log T}{(\varepsilon \vee (S_T / T))^2})$.

results.notes: Bound on attack cost (number of injected samples), with success (zero non-target online pulls) w.p. >= 1-delta. Out-of-scope attacker guarantee.

symbols.Delta_K: mu_K - r_min, gap of target arm's mean from the lower reward bound

conditions: every (0,delta)-successful bounded offline attack on UCB

source.label: thm:attack-cost-ucb-lower
source.quote: Under~\Cref{asp:scaling-assumptions}, fix $\delta\in(0,1/2)$. Let $\Delta_K \triangleq \mu_K - \rl$. For all sufficiently large $T$, every $(0,\delta)$-successful bounded offline attack on UCB satisfies $\mathcal C(\mathbf n)=\Omega(\frac{K\log T}{{(\Delta_K\vee(S_T/T))}^2})$ with probability at least $1-\delta-1/T$.

results.notes: Lower bound on attack cost over attackers, not learners.

bound.regime: Delta_K = o(Lambda_T/T), T sufficiently large; up to a (1+o(1)) factor

source.label: cor:ucb-near-boundary-optimality
source.quote: Under~\Cref{asp:scaling-assumptions}, fix $\delta\in(0,1/2)$ and assume $\Delta_K=o(\Lambda_T/T)$. For all sufficiently large $T$, our construction has $\mathcal C(\mathbf n) \le (1+o(1))\Lambda_T$.

results.notes: Expression is Lambda_T; actual bound is (1+o(1))Lambda_T.

bound.regime: Delta_K = o(Lambda_T/T), T sufficiently large; up to a (1-o(1)) factor

conditions: every (0,delta)-successful bounded offline attack on UCB

source.label: cor:ucb-near-boundary-optimality
source.quote: And every $(0,\delta)$-successful bounded offline attack on UCB satisfies $\Pr[\mathcal C(\mathbf n)\ge(1-o(1))\Lambda_T]\ge1-\delta-\frac1T$.

results.notes: Leading-constant matching lower bound on attack cost.

conditions: every (o(Lambda_T),delta)-successful bounded offline attack on UCB with C(n) <= (1+o(1))Lambda_T

source.label: lem:ucb-allocation-necessity
source.quote: If $\Delta_K = o(\Lambda_T/T)$, then for all sufficiently large $T$, every $(o(\Lambda_T), \delta)$-successful bounded offline attack on UCB with $\mathcal C(\mathbf n) \le (1+o(1)) \Lambda_T$ satisfies $\Pr[n_K = (\frac{2}{3} + o(1)) \Lambda_T]\ge1-\delta-\frac1T$.

results.notes: Quantity is the target-arm injection count n_K (equality up to o(1)), not total cost. Lemma also states construction achieves n_K=(2/3+o(1))Lambda_T.

bound.regime: Delta_K = o(Lambda_T/T), xi = O(Lambda_T), T sufficiently large

conditions: every (xi,delta)-successful bounded offline attack on UCB with a deterministic O(Lambda_T) cost bound

source.label: lem:ucb-target-budget
source.quote: Under~\Cref{asp:scaling-assumptions}, fix $\delta\in(0,1/2)$ and assume $\Delta_K=o(\Lambda_T/T)$ and $\xi=O(\Lambda_T)$. For all sufficiently large $T$, every $(\xi,\delta)$-successful bounded offline attack on UCB with a deterministic $O(\Lambda_T)$ cost bound satisfies $n_K=\Omega(\Lambda_T)$, $\frac{n_K}{\mathcal C(\mathbf n)}=\Omega(1)$ with probability at least $1-\delta-1/T$.

results.notes: Bound on target-arm injection count; also n_K/C = Omega(1).

bound.regime: Delta_K = o(S_T/T), T sufficiently large; up to (1+o(1)) factor

conditions: learner is Gaussian TS sampling N(hat mu_i, 1/N_i)

source.label: thm:attack-cost-ts
source.quote: If $\Delta_K=o(S_T/T)$, there exists a threshold for the above allocation satisfying $\Pr(\sum_{i=1}^{K-1}N_i^\on(T+1)=0)\ge1-2\delta$ and $\mathcal C(\mathbf n)\le(1+o(1))\Lambda_T^{\rm ts}$. Moreover, under $\mathcal E_\delta$, $n_K=(\frac23+o(1))\Lambda_T^{\rm ts}$ ...

results.notes: gamma(T)^2 = 2 log(pi^2 K T^2/(3 delta)) substituted. Also gives allocation n_K = (2/3+o(1)) Lambda_T^ts.

symbols.A_T: sum_{i<K}(N_i^cl + B_i^A), with B_i^A the post-suppression pull bound of the learner

conditions: non-target online pulls bounded by sum_i B_i^A w.p. >= 1-2delta

source.label: thm:pull-count-upper
source.quote: Suppose $\mathcal A$ is suppression-bounded ... There exists a bounded offline attack that satisfies: $\Pr(\sum_{i=1}^{K-1} N_i^{\on} (T + 1) \le \sum_{i = 1}^{K-1} B_i^{\mathcal A}) \ge 1 - 2 \delta$ and $\mathcal C(\mathbf n)\le\mathcal O(\inf_{\rho \in (0, R)} \{K+T\frac{(\rho-\varepsilon)_+}{R-\rho}+\frac{R-\rho}{\rho}\sum_{i=1}^{K-1}(N_i^{\rm cl}+B_i^{\mathcal A})\})$.

results.notes: Theorem states an infimum over rho; recorded the simplified consequence given in the text right after the theorem.

bound.regime: T sufficiently large; up to (2+o(1)) factor

symbols.B_eg: ceil of exploration bound B_i^eg(0,T,delta/(K-1)) for the epsilon-greedy schedule

conditions: learner is epsilon-greedy with deterministic schedule

source.label: thm:attack-cost-eg
source.quote: Fix $\delta\in(0,1/2)$. Suppose $R=\Theta(1)$, $\sum_{s=1}^T\epsilon_s+K\log(K/\delta)=o(T)$. For all sufficiently large $T$, the above attack satisfies $\Pr(\sum_{i<K}N_i^\on(T+1)\le(K-1)B)\ge1-\delta$, $\mathcal C(\mathbf n)=(2+o(1))\sqrt{T(K-1)B}$.

results.notes: For eps_s = min{1, cK/s} gives cost O(sqrt(T K log T)).
